audit.whatIsWrong: The early-lane difficulty read says walking up means eating 'his passive crit autos'. Trial by Fire is not a crit — it is a periodic melee strike that sets the target on fire.
audit.why: Riot's text for Trial by Fire: 'Every few seconds, Gangplank's melee strike will set his opponent on fire.' It is a damage-over-time proc, not a critical strike. A Rumble player told to fear crits at level 1 will over-respect a burn tick and give up the free chip that actually decides the level-1 neutral. It also hides the real level-1 threat, which is Parrrley at 625 range on a 4.5-second cooldown.
audit.corrected: Trial by Fire is a burn on his melee strike, not a crit. The level-1 pressure comes from Parrrley — 625 range, flat 4.5s — poking you while he last-hits.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike says 'his W cleanse means your E slow gets eaten' with no cooldown, so it reads as a permanent loss of your kite tool.
audit.why: Remove Scurvy is 22/20/18/16/14s and costs 60 to 100 mana. It is a single answer on a long cooldown, not a standing immunity. The spike is real but it is a 22-second window at rank 1: he cleanses once and then has nearly half a minute where your harpoon slow sticks and he still has no dash.
audit.corrected: Remove Scurvy is 22s at rank 1 falling to 14s. Bait it, then run the pattern in the window behind it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interaction errors. (a) wants.you[1] and whys[1] both say Electro Harpoon 'grounds' Gangplank. It does not — it is a slow, and nothing in Rumble's kit grounds. (b) The early text claims 'Remove Scurvy does not remove the harpoon slow retroactively if he waits to use it'. Remove Scurvy cures crowd control effects, so casting it does clear an already-applied harpoon slow.
audit.why: Grounding is a specific mechanic that stops dashes; Rumble has none, and Gangplank has no dash for it to stop. Telling a player their slow 'grounds' him invents a lock that never lands. And the cleanse claim is backwards: the counterplay is not that he must pre-cast, it is that Remove Scurvy is on a 22-second cooldown and cannot answer two harpoons and a 3-second Flamespitter burn in the same window.
audit.corrected: Electro Harpoon slows him and shreds his MR — it does not ground. He has no dash, so a slow is enough. Remove Scurvy cures the slow when he casts it, but it is 22s at rank 1: force it, then commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block tracks only Powder Keg and gives no numbers, and Powder Keg is written as 'Powder Kegs' throughout the page.
audit.why: Riot's ability name is Powder Keg, singular. Data Dragon reports its cooldown as 0 because it is charge-based, so no number can be quoted for it — but the two cooldowns that actually gate this lane can be: Remove Scurvy 22 to 14s and Parrrley a flat 4.5s. Cannon Barrage is 160/140/120s.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block now tracks Remove Scurvy at 22 to 14s alongside Powder Keg, and uses the singular ability name.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing, despite Remove Scurvy restoring health on every cast.
audit.why: _missing-interactions flags needs-antiheal for this pairing and Riot's text confirms the heal. Against a poke-versus-poke lane, anti-heal is what stops him resetting your chip every 22 seconds.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into the first-item spike alongside the Remove Scurvy cooldown.

edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely neutral — Gangplank throws a Powder Keg from outside your 600 cone and pokes with Parrrley at 625 on a flat 4.5 seconds. His Trial by Fire is a burn on his melee strike, not a crit, so the thing to fear is the barrel, not the auto. Hover at max Q range and pop any keg he pre-places so he does not get the gold. At Level 2 double Electro Harpoon changes the equation: when the keg is spent, walk up, Flamespitter at Danger Zone heat, and land both harpoons — he has no dash, so a slow is all you need. Remove Scurvy will cure it, but that is 22 seconds at rank 1. By Level 3 the wave is yours whenever the keg is down; the moment you see it on cooldown, step in.
edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely neutral — Gangplank can throw a Powder Kegs barrel from just outside your Flamespitter cone and you cannot punish it without walking into his passive crit autos. Do not overextend; instead, hover at max Q range and pop any barrel he pre-places so he does not get the gold. At Level 2, your double Electro-Harpoon changes the equation: when his Powder Kegs is on cooldown, walk up, fire Flamespitter at Danger Zone heat, and hit him with both E casts before he can walk out — he has no dash and Remove Scurvy does not remove the harpoon slow retroactively if he waits to use it. By Level 3, the wave belongs to you as long as Powder Kegs is down; the moment you see the barrel icon on cooldown, step in.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a discipline check: he can chain two or three kegs into real poke, and Scrap Shield does not absorb a full detonation the way it handles single-target damage. Trade strictly on Powder Keg windows — when he blows kegs on minions or you pop one, that is your green light for Flamespitter at Danger Zone heat. Force Remove Scurvy early in the trade and the next 22 seconds belong to your harpoon slow, because he has no dash to leave with. At Level 6 The Equalizer shifts the macro: even in a dead-even lane, a wall laid into a river skirmish or across a gank path creates immediate kill pressure that Cannon Barrage cannot match. Freeze near your side so he must walk in to contest CS.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a discipline check: Gangplank can now chain two or three barrels for a significant poke pattern, and your W shield does NOT negate burst damage from a full barrel detonation the way it handles single-target damage. Trade strictly on Powder Kegs cooldown windows — when he blows barrels on minions or you pop one, that is your green light to commit Flamespitter. At Level 6 your Equalizer shifts the macro entirely: even if the lane is dead even, a well-placed Equalizer into a river skirmish or on top of a jungler gank path creates kill pressure that Gangplank's own global R cannot match in immediate lethality. Keep the wave frozen near your side so he has to walk into your pattern to contest CS.

edits.after: From first item Gangplank's Trinity Force crits start to hurt and Remove Scurvy reliably cures your Electro Harpoon slow, so the clean pattern gets rarer — but it is still one cleanse on 22 down to 14 seconds, and Grievous Wounds turns the heal attached to it into nothing. At 2+ items his keg crits chunk you before Flamespitter's burn adds up, and Cannon Barrage is 160 seconds of global objective pressure that rivals your Equalizer. Shift to front-lining with Equalizer as the engage. Your grouped damage still matters; stop hunting the solo kill on a completed Gangplank and let the burning wall do the work while your carries follow.
edits.before: First item onwards, Gangplank's Trinity Force or Essence Reaver crits start to hurt and his Remove Scurvy reliably eats your Electro-Harpoon slow, so your window to chain a clean pattern shrinks significantly. At 2+ items, his barrel crits can one-shot or severely chunk you before you get Flamespitter sustained damage online, and his Cannon Barrage provides global teamfight pressure that rivals your Equalizer. Shift your role to front-lining teamfights with Equalizer as the engage tool — your damage in a grouped fight still matters, but stop trying to solo-kill a Gangplank who has completed his core; instead let your AoE ultimate do the work and let your carries follow the burning wall.

notes: Riot's ability name is Powder Keg, singular — the page used 'Powder Kegs' throughout; the strings I rewrote now use the correct name, but many untouched strings on this matchup still carry the plural. Two other real errors fixed: Trial by Fire was described as 'passive crit autos' when it is a burn on his melee strike, and Electro Harpoon was said to 'ground' him when it only slows (nothing in Rumble's kit grounds, and Gangplank has no dash to ground anyway). The page also claimed Remove Scurvy cannot retroactively remove the harpoon slow — it cures crowd control on cast, so it can; the real counterplay is its 22-to-14s cooldown. Powder Keg's cooldown reads as 0 in Data Dragon because it is charge-based, so I quoted no number for it. The _missing-interactions entry 'Gangplank bypasses stacking resistances (Cannon Barrage R)' is a misfire — Cannon Barrage is ordinary damage and a slow — and was not written.
